---
title: "Brainstorm Creative Story Prompts for Your Hobby Novel Using Cohere"
subtitle: "Unlock fresh ideas for your next story or project by using an AI assistant to spark your imagination and overcome writer's block."
category: "guide"
audience: "personal"
company: "Cohere"
tool: "Cohere"
level: "beginner"
read_time_minutes: 6
tags: ["getting-started", "creative-writing", "brainstorming"]
---

Feeling stuck on your next great story idea? Whether you're a budding novelist, a tabletop game master, or just love creating worlds, sometimes the well of inspiration runs dry. This guide will show you how to use Cohere, an AI assistant, to generate a flood of creative story prompts and get your imagination flowing again, step-by-step.

## Before you start
- **A Cohere account:** You can sign up for a free account on the Cohere website. This usually gives you access to their "Playground" for experimentation.
- **A web browser:** Like Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge.
- **About 10-15 minutes:** To explore the tool and generate your first batch of ideas.

## Step 1 — Access the Cohere Playground
First, open your web browser and navigate to the Cohere website. Once you've logged in, you'll need to find your way to the "Playground". Think of the Playground as a digital sandbox where you can try out different AI models without needing any complicated setup. It's designed for easy experimentation.

You'll usually see a navigation menu on the left side of the screen. Look for an option labelled "Playground" or something similar. Click on it to enter.

If it looks different: The exact layout can change, but generally, main navigation items are on the left. If you don't see "Playground", look for "Console," "API," or "Dashboard" and then explore those menus for "Playground" or "Demo."

You'll know it worked when you see a main content area with a large text box where you can type, often alongside some settings options.

## Step 2 — Select an AI Model
Inside the Playground, you'll work with an AI **model**, which is like a specialised digital brain trained to understand and generate text. Cohere offers a few different models, each with slightly different strengths. For brainstorming story ideas, a general-purpose text generation model works best.

Look for a dropdown menu, often near the top or side of the main text area, labelled "Model" or "Base Model". Click on this menu and select a model like "Command" or "Command-R". These are great for creative tasks.

If it looks different: If "Command" isn't available, choose the most recent 'Command' variant or a model described as good for general language generation. Avoid models specifically for "Embed" or "Rerank" as they're for different tasks.

You'll know it worked when the selected model's name appears in the dropdown menu, confirming it's ready for your input.

## Step 3 — Write Your Initial Idea
Now it's time to give the AI its first instruction, also known as a **prompt**. This is the starting point for your brainstorming. Think about any small flicker of an idea you have – a character, a setting, a genre, or even just a mood. The more context you provide, even if it's brief, the better.

Locate the large text box, typically labelled "Prompt", "Input", or "Text". Type in a sentence or two about what kind of story ideas you're looking for. Don't worry about perfection; this is just to get started.

If it looks different: The input box might be titled "Chat" if the Playground is set up for conversational interactions, but it still works the same for single prompts. Just type your instruction directly.

💬 Example: `I'm writing a fantasy novel about a lost princess, but I need some fresh ideas for her quest. Give me 5 unique story prompts.`

You'll know it worked when your text appears in the input box, ready for the AI to process.

## Step 4 — Refine the Instructions for Better Prompts
To get truly useful and creative prompts, you'll want to add some detail to your instructions. Think about what makes your story unique. Are there specific elements you want to include or avoid? Adding constraints or preferences helps the AI narrow its focus and generate more tailored ideas.

Go back to your prompt in the text box. Add more descriptive words about the princess, the world she lives in, or the challenges you envision. This helps the AI understand your vision better.

If it looks different: Some Playgrounds might have separate fields for "System Message" or "Instructions." If so, put your general request in the main prompt box and any overarching rules or persona requests in the "System Message" area.

💬 Example: `I'm writing a fantasy novel about a lost princess in a world where magic is slowly fading. She needs to embark on a quest to restore it, but she's not a warrior. Give me 5 unique story prompts focusing on cunning, diplomacy, or discovery.`

You'll know it worked when your updated, more detailed prompt is visible in the input box.

## Step 5 — Generate and Review Prompts
With your detailed prompt ready, it's time to unleash the AI! The model will process your instructions and generate text based on what it thinks you're looking for. This is where the magic happens, transforming your initial thoughts into concrete story ideas.

Find and click a button usually labelled "Generate," "Run," "Submit," or "Send." This will send your prompt to the Cohere model. After a moment, the AI's response will appear in an output area, usually below or to the side of your input.

If it looks different: The "Generate" button might be an arrow icon or a simple "Enter" key press if you're in a chat-like interface. Be patient, it might take a few seconds for the AI to process your request.

You'll know it worked when you see a list of numbered story prompts or distinct paragraphs of ideas appear in the output section.

## Step 6 — Iterate for More Ideas or Different Angles
The first set of prompts is a great start, but AI is best used iteratively – meaning you try, you review, and then you tweak your request for even better results. If the ideas aren't quite hitting the mark, don't worry! You can easily ask for more or guide the AI in a new direction.

You have a few options:
1.  **Ask for more:** Type a follow-up like "Give me 3 more ideas, but make them darker."
2.  **Refine a specific idea:** Copy one of the generated prompts you like and ask the AI to "Expand on this idea: [pasted prompt]" or "Give me variations of this quest."
3.  **Adjust the temperature/creativity setting:** Many Playgrounds have a "Temperature" or "Creativity" slider (a **setting** that controls how adventurous or wild the AI's output is). Drag it up for more imaginative ideas, or down for more focused ones.

After making your change, click "Generate" again.

You'll know it worked when the AI provides new or refined prompts, building on your previous conversation or new instructions.

## Common mistakes
-   **Too vague prompts:** If you just say "Write a story idea," the AI will give you generic ideas.
    *   **The fix:** Be specific! Mention genre, character type, key conflicts, or desired tone. "Give me a sci-fi prompt about a rogue AI protecting a small colony" is much better.
-   **Expecting a perfect novel:** The AI provides prompts, not full stories. It's a brainstorming partner, not a ghostwriter for your entire book.
    *   **The fix:** Use the prompts as jumping-off points. Take an idea you like and develop it further with your own creativity and unique voice.
-   **Not iterating enough:** Sometimes the first answer isn't perfect, and that's okay. People often forget they can keep talking to the AI.
    *   **The fix:** Don't be afraid to ask for more ideas, clarify what you didn't like, or suggest a new angle based on the AI's previous response.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** If you're a hobby writer, this means no more staring at a blank page. You can quickly generate ideas for fanfiction, D&D campaigns, or even just creative writing exercises to keep your skills sharp.
-   **For your business or work:** While focused on novels here, the same approach can spark ideas for marketing campaigns, blog post topics, or creative solutions to project challenges. It's a versatile tool for any brainstorming need.
-   **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to pick a genre you love and ask for three short story ideas within it. For example: "Give me 3 whimsical fantasy short story prompts."

## Try it now
Open Cohere's Playground, select the "Command" model, and enter this prompt: "I'm interested in writing a detective story set in a unique location. Give me 3 creative mystery plot ideas, focusing on the setting itself as a key part of the puzzle." Hit 'Generate' and see what fascinating mysteries it uncovers!
